solution:
Write the expression as x2+(k+2)x+1−2k. Because its x2 coefficient is 1, it is positive for all real x precisely when its discriminant is negative.

The discriminant is (k+2)2−4(1−2k)=k2+12k=k(k+12). The inequality k(k+12)<0 holds exactly between the roots −12 and 0.

Thus −12<k<0, option A. At either endpoint the quadratic touches zero, so the strict condition excludes them. Equivalently, its minimum is −k(k+12)4, which is positive on exactly this interval.
knowledgePattern: Require negative discriminant for an upward quadratic positive everywhere
